 1                                         INTRODUCTION

 2          1.      Since no later than October 2023 and continuing through at least June 2024,

 3   Defendants Judang Team LLC (“Judang Team”), Perfeos LLC d/b/a Shop at Mars (“Perfeos”),

 4   and Antonio José Liévano (“Liévano”), individually and acting through Judang Team, Perfeos,

 5   and his unincorporated business Jot & Journeys (“J&J”), (collectively, “Defendants”) operated a

 6   deceptive and misleading advertising scheme on Facebook and Instagram.

 7          2.      Defendants used fraudulent financial documents to improperly obtain more than $8

 8   million in advertising credit lines from Meta for which they never paid Meta. Defendants used the

 9   fraudulently obtained advertising credit lines to purchase ads on Facebook and Instagram

10   promoting a variety of merchandise. When a Facebook or Instagram user clicked on one of

11   Defendants’ ads, the users were redirected to websites operated by Defendants, including

12   shopatmars.com. After placing orders though Defendants’ websites, users received merchandise

13   that was different and of lesser quality than what Defendants advertised or did not receive any

14   merchandise at all. This practice is known as a “bait-and-switch” scheme. Additionally, several

15   Facebook and Instagram users who placed an order on Defendants’ websites received recurring,

16   unauthorized charges on their credit cards. This practice is known as “subscription fraud.”

17   Defendants took steps to conceal their fraudulent schemes, including by blocking customer

18   complaints and negative product reviews placed on Defendants’ Facebook Pages, and creating

19   fake financial records.
20          3.      Defendants’ actions violate Meta’s Terms of Service (“Meta’s Terms”),

21   Instagram’s Terms of Use (“Instagram’s Terms”), Meta’s Advertising Standards (“Meta’s Ad

22   Standards”), Meta’s Commercial Terms (“Meta’s Commercial Terms”), Meta’s Self-Service

23   Advertising Terms (“Meta’s Self-Serve Ad Terms”), and Meta’s Facebook Online Invoicing

24   Terms and Conditions (“Meta’s Online Invoicing Terms”) (collectively, “Meta’s and Instagram’s

25   Terms and Policies”); and California law. Meta previously (a) took technical enforcement actions

26   against Defendants’ advertisements, advertising accounts, Facebook Pages, and user accounts; (b)

27   sent a cease-and-desist letter to Defendants that demanded they stop violating Meta’s and

28   Instagram’s Terms and Policies and provide payment for outstanding ad credit line balances; and
                                                  2
                                              COMPLAINT
             Case 3:25-cv-05156-TSH            Document 1     Filed 06/18/25      Page 3 of 25




 1   (c) revoked Defendants’ access to Meta services, including Facebook and Instagram.

 2   Subsequently, and in further violation of Meta’s Terms and Instagram’s Terms, Defendants created

 3   new Facebook and Instagram accounts and continued using Facebook and Instagram. Meta now

 4   brings this action for a permanent injunction that prohibits Defendants from continuing their bait

 5   and switch and subscription schemes, and to recover damages.

 6                                              PARTIES

 7          4.      Plaintiff Meta is a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business in

 8   Menlo Park, San Mateo County, California. Meta owns and operates several services, including

 9   Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.

10          5.      Defendant Judang Team is a Florida Corporation, with a principal address at 1915

11   Northeast 20th Avenue, Fort Lauderdale, Florida 33305. On its website, judangteam.com, Judang

12   Team promotes itself as a social media manager, purporting to “manage[] content that averages

13   over 1 billion views per month across its channels and influencer partnerships.”

14          6.      Defendant Perfeos is a Florida Corporation, with a principal address at 2916 North

15   Miami Avenue, Miami, Florida 33127. On its website, shopatmars.com, Perfeos purports to sell

16   various merchandise.

17          7.      Defendant J&J is an unincorporated Florida business, with purported addresses at

18   121 Northeast 34th Street, Miami, Florida 33137 and 2916 North Miami Avenue, Miami, Florida

19   33127. On its website, jotandjourney.com, J&J purports to sell various consumer goods including
20   stationary products and energy drinks.

21          8.      Defendant Liévano is a resident of Miami, Florida. Upon information and belief,

22   Liévano is the founder and sole member of Judang Team and Perfeos. He also operates J&J. On

23   his LinkedIn page, Liévano claims to have “[r]ecord” eCommerce sales ranging from $475,000 to

24   $826,000 “in a Day.”

17          9.      On information and belief, at all times material to this action, Defendants were the

18   agents, employees, and/or co-conspirators with each of the remaining Defendants and were acting

19   within the scope of such agency, employment, and/or conspiracy. At all times material to this

20   action, each Defendant was the agent of the other Defendant. Each Defendant acted with the

21   knowledge, permission, and consent of the other Defendant; and each Defendant aided and abetted

22   the other Defendant in the acts or omissions alleged in this Complaint.

23                                   JURISDICTION AND VENUE

24          10.     The Court has jurisdiction over all the causes of action alleged in this Complaint

25   pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1332 because complete diversity between Plaintiff and Defendants exists,

26   and because the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.

27          11.     The Court has personal jurisdiction over Defendants because Defendants created,

28   controlled, and used multiple Facebook and Instagram accounts and thereby had notice of and

                                                  4
                                              COMPLAINT
             Case 3:25-cv-05156-TSH           Document 1       Filed 06/18/25     Page 5 of 25




 1   agreed to Meta’s Terms and Meta’s Commercial Terms, which contain a forum selection clause

 2   that requires Defendants to submit to the jurisdiction of the U.S. District Court for the Northern

 3   District of California or a state court located in San Mateo County.

 4          12.     The Court also has personal jurisdiction because Defendants purposefully directed

 5   their conduct at Plaintiff, which has its principal place of business in California. For example,

 6   Defendants requested ad credit lines from Meta, a California business, and then purposefully used

 7   Meta’s ad services to purchase and run deceptive and misleading advertisements on Facebook and

 8   Instagram using that credit. Additionally, Defendants purposefully directed their misleading and

 9   deceptive ads at Facebook and Instagram users in California, and Facebook and Instagram users

10   in California actually clicked on those ads and purchased defective, low-quality, and misleading

11   products that were part of Defendants’ bait-and-switch scheme. Plaintiff’s claims arise directly

12   from and relate to these California contacts.

13          13.     Venue is proper in this judicial district pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b) as the

14   threatened and actual harm to the Plaintiff occurred in this district. Additionally, by agreeing to

15   the forum selection clause, Defendants agreed that venue in this Court is proper.

16          14.     Pursuant to Civil L.R. 3-2(c & d), this case may be assigned to either the San

17   Francisco or Oakland division because Meta is located in San Mateo County.

18                                     FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS

19          1. Background on Meta
20          15.     Meta owns and operates Facebook, which is an online service that is available on

21   computers and mobile devices which helps give people the power to build community, share life’s

22   moments and discuss what is happening, and discover and connect to interests through Feed, Reels,

23   Stories, Groups, Marketplace, and more.

24          16.     Meta also owns and operates Instagram, which is a free photo and video sharing

25   service and mobile application. Instagram users can upload photos and videos to Instagram and

26   share them with others. They can also view, comment, and like on posts shared by others on

27   Instagram.

28
                                                   5
                                               COMPLAINT
             Case 3:25-cv-05156-TSH           Document 1        Filed 06/18/25        Page 6 of 25




 1          17.      Meta also owns WhatsApp, an encrypted communication service available on

 2   mobile devices and desktop computers. WhatsApp relies on Meta’s infrastructure, such as servers,

 3   to support people around the world with fast, reliable, and private services.

 4          18.     In addition to Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, Meta also operates various

 5   business and advertising services (collectively, “Meta’s Services”).

 6          2. Advertising on Facebook and Instagram

 7          19.     At all relevant times, including from October 2023 to June 2024, businesses and

 8   individuals with a Facebook or Instagram account could create and place ads on Facebook and

 9   Instagram.

10          20.     To create and publish an ad on Facebook, an advertiser must agree to Meta’s Terms,

11   Meta’s Self-Serve Ad Terms, Meta’s Commercial Terms, and Meta’s Ad Standards. To advertise

12   on Instagram, an advertiser must additionally agree to Instagram’s Terms. Advertisers are also

13   subject to Meta’s Community Standards and Instagram’s Community Guidelines.

14          21.     Certain business accounts are eligible to apply for ad credit lines. Once approved,

15   advertisers are provided a credit line for limited ad costs, which represents the maximum amount

16   a business could spend on ads on a monthly basis before payment is required. Monthly invoices

17   are provided for any ads purchased using these credit lines and are payable within 30 days of

18   issuing. Businesses may seek modifications to their credit lines, for instance, to increase limits.

19          22.     Meta periodically reviews products sold through ads placed on Facebook and
20   Instagram. Meta’s review includes solicitation of feedback from a random sample of customers

21   that purchased products after clicking on an ad on Facebook or Instagram. Meta also employs

22   shoppers to purchase products through ads placed on Facebook or Instagram and provide feedback

23   on their experiences.

24          23.     Meta can take a range of enforcement actions against an advertiser who violates

25   Meta’s and Instagram’s Terms and Policies, including banning an ad account from running ads or

26   disabling all Facebook and Instagram accounts belonging to an advertiser.

27          24.     A Facebook Page is a public page on Facebook designed for businesses,

28   organizations, and public figures. Only a Facebook user can create or manage a Facebook
                                                   6
                                               COMPLAINT

 1   Page. Facebook Pages are managed by Facebook users who have the role of administrators or

 2   moderators.

 3            25.   Page administrators and moderators can create and run ads and promotions on

 4   behalf of their Facebook Pages.

 5            26.   Any Facebook user can leave comments on a Facebook Page. Facebook Page

 6   administrators and moderators, however, have the ability to control the content users post on their

 7   Page. Administrators or moderators can choose to block specific words or phrases from appearing

 8   on their Facebook Pages. When someone comments on a Page using a word that the Page

 9   administrator or moderator has blocked, the comment is hidden from the Page.

10            3. Meta’s and Instagram’s Terms and Policies

11                  A.      Meta’s Terms

12            27.   Everyone who uses Facebook must agree to Meta’s Terms (available at

13   https://www.facebook.com/terms.php) and other rules that govern access to and use of Facebook

14   (collectively, “Meta’s Terms and Policies”).

15            28.   At all relevant times, Meta’s Terms have prohibited, among other things, violations

16   of Meta’s Community Standards (see https://transparency.meta.com/policies/community-

17   standards), Meta’s Ad Standards (see https://transparency.meta.com/policies/ad-standards/), and

18   Meta’s Commercial Terms (see https://facebook.com/legal/commercial_terms) (“Meta’s

19   Commercial Terms”).
20            29.   Meta’s Terms prohibit users from doing or sharing anything “that is unlawful,

21   misleading, discriminatory or fraudulent (or assists someone else in using our Products in such a

22   way).”

23            30.   Meta’s Terms prohibit users from doing anything to “impair the proper working,

24   integrity, operation, or appearance of our services, systems, or Products.”

25            31.   Meta’s Terms state that a person cannot use Facebook if Meta “previously disabled

26   your account for violations of our Terms, the Community Standards, or other terms and policies

27   that apply to your use of Facebook.”

 1                   B.         Instagram’s Terms

 2           32.     At all relevant times, everyone who used Instagram agreed to Instagram’s Terms

 3   (see https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870) and to other rules that govern access to and

 4   use of Instagram, including Instagram’s Community Guidelines and Platform Policies

 5   (collectively, “Instagram’s Terms and Policies”).

 6           33.     Instagram’s Terms prohibit users from doing “anything unlawful, misleading, or

 7   fraudulent or for an illegal or unauthorized purpose.”

 8           34.     Instagram’s Terms prohibit users from doing “anything to interfere with or impair

 9   the intended operation of [Instagram].”

10           35.     Instagram’s Terms state that a person cannot use Instagram if Meta has previously

11   disabled the user’s account for violating any of Meta’s policies.

12                   C.         Meta’s Commercial Terms, Ad Standards, Self-Serve Ad Terms, and

13                              Online Invoicing Terms

14           36.     At all relevant times, Meta’s Commercial Terms applied to access or use of Meta

15   products for a business or commercial purpose, including “using ads, selling products,” and

16   “managing a Page.” Meta’s Commercial Terms equally apply to activities Meta users perform on

17   behalf of third parties.

18           37.     When accessing Meta’s services on behalf of a third party, Meta’s Commercial

19   Terms require a user to “ensure that any third party on whose behalf [they] access or use any Meta
20   Product for any business or commercial purpose will abide by the applicable terms of use,

21   including these Commercial Terms, the Meta Terms of Service (‘Terms’), and any applicable

22   supplemental terms.” They must also “represent and warrant that [they] have the authority to bind

23   that third party to such terms.”

24           38.     Meta’s Commercial Terms require that “access or use of the Meta products for

25   business or commercial purposes complies with all applicable laws, rules, and regulations.”

26           39.     At all relevant times, Meta’s Ad Standards “appl[ied] to (1) ads and commercial

27   content served by or purchased through Meta . . . , (2) ads appearing within apps on Meta [e.g.,

 1   Facebook], and (3) ads on Instagram.” Meta’s Ad Standards equally apply to ads Meta users create

 2   and run, or cause to be created and run, on behalf of third parties.

 3          40.     Meta’s Ad Standards “prohibit ads promoting products, services, schemes or offers

 4   using deceptive or misleading practices, including those meant to scam people out of money or

 5   personal information.”

 6          41.     At      all   relevant   times,   Meta’s   Self-Serve   Ad   Terms    (available   at

 7   https://www.facebook.com/legal/self_service_ads_terms) applied to “use of Meta Products (such

 8   as the self-service advertising interfaces and APIs) for creation, submission and/or delivery of any

 9   advertising or other commercial or sponsored activity or content (collectively, ‘Self-Serve Ad

10   Interfaces’) . . . and any order you place through the Self-Serve Ad Interfaces (‘Order’).”

11          42.     Meta’s Self-Serve Ad Terms state that “ads must comply with all applicable laws,

12   regulations, and guidelines, as well as our Advertising [Standards]” and that “[f]ailure to comply

13   may result in a variety of consequences, including the cancellation of ads you have placed and

14   termination of your account.”

15          43.     Meta’s Self-Serve Ad Terms require payment of “all amounts specified in each

16   Order you place, along with any applicable taxes.” Meta’s Self-Serve Ad Terms equally apply to

17   ads Meta users create and run, or cause to be created and run, on behalf of third parties.

18          44.     Meta’s Self-Serve Ad Terms provide notice that if an “account is past due, we may

19   take additional steps to collect past due amounts. You will pay all expenses associated with such
20   collection, including reasonable attorneys’ fees. Past due amounts will accrue interest at 1% per

21   month or the lawful maximum, whichever is less.”

22          45.     At all relevant times, Meta’s Facebook Online Invoicing Terms and Conditions

23   (available upon log in at https://business.facebook.com/terms_ads_invoicing.php) (“Meta’s

24   Online Invoicing Terms”) applied in addition to Meta’s Self-Serve Ad Terms “[w]ith respect to

25   any Order that you place through Facebook’s online advertising portal for which Facebook agrees

26   to invoice you.” For such orders, Meta’s Self-Serve Ad Terms, as modified by Meta’s Online

27   Invoicing Terms, require that users “make all payments within thirty (30) days of the date of the

28   applicable invoice.”

15           4. Defendants Bait-and-Switch and Subscription Schemes

16           54.      Since no later than October 2023, Defendants facilitated bait-and-switch and

17   subscription fraud schemes using Facebook and Instagram ads targeted at Facebook and Instagram

18   users in, among other countries, the United States. Defendants’ schemes proceeded generally in

19   five steps:
20                    a.     Defendants fraudulently obtained advertising credit lines and credit line

21   increases from Meta, including by using fraudulent financial records.

22                    b.     Defendants used the fraudulently obtained advertising credit lines to place

23   ads on Facebook and Instagram, including through Facebook Pages under their control, promoting

24   the sale of various merchandise. Users who clicked on these ads were then taken to Defendants’

25   websites to order and pay for the advertised merchandise.

26                    c.     After users placed orders on Defendants’ websites, Defendants either sent

27   products to those users that were different and of inferior quality or never sent the merchandise.

28

             Case 3:25-cv-05156-TSH              Document 1       Filed 06/18/25      Page 13 of 25




 1                     d.       Defendants charged recurring subscription fees to users that those users did

 2   not authorize.

 3                     e.       Defendants took steps to conceal their schemes, including by blocking and

 4   removing customer complaints and negative reviews from their Facebook Pages. The removal of

 5   these negative comments was designed to mislead, deceive, and misrepresent the true nature of the

 6   products by concealing negative comments by users that exposed Defendants’ bait-and-switch

 7   scheme.

 8                     A.       Defendants Used False and Materially Misleading Documents and

 9                              Statements to Induce Meta to Provide More Than $8.1 Million in Ad

10                              Credit Lines

11          55.        Defendants funded their bait-and-switch and subscription schemes, in part, by

12   defrauding Meta. Defendants knowingly submitted false and materially misleading documents

13   and made false and misleading statements in order to induce Meta into providing multiple credit

14   line increases.        Meta reasonably and justifiably relied on Defendants’ false and materially

15   misleading information, ultimately providing them more than $8.1 million in ad credit lines.

16   Defendants spent to the limits of their ad credit lines and have not repaid the outstanding balance.

24   subsequently submitted to Meta on or about May 27, 2024 to obtain yet another advertising credit

25   line increase.
